review_comments: Any specific reason it should be in a constructor and not assigned on declaration as other fields?
Putting `= new MsQuicBuffers()` in the field initializer triggers "Don't assign default values" or similar warning, and leaving it uninitialized breaks because the `MsQuicBuffers._handles` is null.
Why did you merge the two `if`s into one here? Or why not get rid of the `_count` and use `_handles.Length` instead?

The size of `_buffers` is always the same as `_handles`, so they will either both grow or neither of them will.

`_count` contains the number of valid/used slots in those arrays, depending on history, it may be lower than `_handles.Length`
